name: incident-review
description: Walkthrough of an outage timeline. Exercises sequence diagrams and flowcharts: actors, ordered calls, a failure path.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Let me walk the timeline and then we talk causes. Nobody jump ahead to fixes.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: 14:02, the deploy of the gateway goes out. Normal rolling deploy, three pods at a time.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And that deploy included the new auth middleware.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Correct. 14:04 the gateway starts calling the auth service on every request instead of using the cached token.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Which is roughly a forty times increase in traffic to auth.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: 14:05 auth service latency goes from twelve milliseconds to eight hundred. 14:06 the auth service connection pool to Postgres is exhausted.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And at that point auth starts returning five hundreds, not timeouts.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Right, and here is the bad part. The gateway treats a five hundred from auth as a denied request rather than an error, so users got logged out instead of getting an error page.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That is what generated the support spike. People thought their accounts were gone.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: 14:11 first alert fires, on support ticket volume, not on any of our service metrics.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That is six minutes of nothing. Auth latency should have paged at 14:05.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: The latency alert exists. It has a ten minute window so it had not tripped yet.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: 14:14 I got paged, 14:19 we identified the deploy as the trigger, 14:22 rollback started, 14:27 fully recovered.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: So twenty five minutes total, nineteen of it user visible.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Causes. The middleware change removed the cache lookup, that is the trigger. But the gateway mapping five hundred to denied is the thing that turned a slow site into a logout event.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the connection pool had no ceiling per caller, so auth had no way to shed load.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Three separate things then. The change, the error mapping, the missing backpressure.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Four. The alerting window meant we found out from customers.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Four, yes. Now fixes.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Error mapping is a one line fix and it is the one that would have made this invisible to users. That first.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Alert window down to two minutes, that is a config change.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Backpressure on auth is the real work. Per caller concurrency limit, shed with a four twenty nine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And a canary step in the gateway deploy so one pod takes traffic for five minutes before the rest go.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: That is the list. Error mapping and alert window today, backpressure and canary this sprint.
